author: Eddie Nolan

evidence.note: P2728R7 shows the author(s) proposing standard UTF transcoding views that sanitize invalid input with U+FFFD and expose an iterator success() accessor, while explicitly arguing in §5.2 that SG16's rejection of char/wchar_t ranges 'is a mistake'.
evidence.title: Unicode in the Library, Part 1: UTF Transcoding (P2728R7)
evidence.what_changed: Between R7 and R14 the changelog (11.7) records 'Remove support for char and wchar_t', a concession of the very position R7's §5.2 defended; R7's iterator success()/utf_transcoding_error error handling was also later reworked into the _or_error views returning std::expected.

evidence.note: P2728R9 confirms the author's settled direction: transcoding views plus or_error views whose value type is std::expected, with wording for [range.transcoding] and code unit adaptors.
evidence.title: Unicode in the Library, Part 1: UTF Transcoding (P2728R9)
evidence.what_changed: Per the R14 changelog (11.5, changes since R9), the author replaced the three to_utfX_view classes in R9 with a single to_utf_view class with constructor tags 'per SG9 feedback from Kona 2025', and replaced the bool OrError CTP with a to_utf_view_error_kind enum; later (11.2) they added views::as_char/as_wchar_t and removed base() for input ranges.

evidence.note: Official SG16 minutes circulated by Tom Honermann record consensus 'in favor' of a P2728 without eager algorithms and strong consensus that UTF transcoding interfaces should operate on charN_t types. The R14 changelog shows the author then acted on this (11.14: 'Remove each eager algorithm'; 11.7: 'Remove support for char and wchar_t').
evidence.title: SG16 meeting summary for April 12th, 2023

position: Eddie Nolan (and Zach Laine, who authored R1-R6) has consistently pursued standard-library UTF transcoding views/ranges across every revision of P2728, with replacement of invalid subsequences by U+FFFD and an error-visible variant. The author's position evolved under committee pressure: after SG16's April 2023 polls, the author dropped eager algorithms and eventually (between R7 and R14) conceded on removing char/wchar_t support, a position R7's design discussion had explicitly defended as 'a mistake'. Error handling also moved from R7's iterator-level success()/utf_transcoding_error to the current _or_error views returning std::expected, following an unofficial SG9 recommendation during Wrocław 2024. The Kona 2025 SG9 poll minutes, as reproduced in R14's relevant-polls section, further show the author continuing to shape the design in response to polls (e.g. consensus to ban char arrays as input and to adopt a single template view class).
recommendation: The paper proposes adding views and ranges to the C++ standard library for transcoding between UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32. It introduces transcoding views that replace invalid subsequences with the replacement character �, as well as _or_error views that report errors via std::expected.
title: Unicode in the Library, Part 1: UTF Transcoding
